resale_co.name: Continued Certificate of Occupancy (Residential Resale housing inspection)
resale_co.issued_by: Housing Officer, Construction Code Office (Department of Code Enforcement / Bureau of Housing Inspections)
resale_co.lead_time: No minimum stated. The fee must be paid in full before an inspection is scheduled; the clerk calls to set an appointment within 5 working days of payment.
requirements: Smoke alarms on every level, in each bedroom and within 10 feet outside each sleeping area (10-year sealed battery type)
Carbon monoxide alarm in the hallway within 10 feet of the bedrooms
Fire extinguisher 2A-10BC, under 10 pounds, mounted within 10 feet of the kitchen in plain sight, tagged or with a current receipt, top no higher than 5 feet
House numbers at least 4 inches and visible from the street
Handrails on stairs with 3 or more risers; guardrails with spindles no more than 4 inches apart on porches or decks 30 inches or higher
GFCI outlets within 6 feet of any water source or the breaker panel
Electric properly installed with no bare wires; heat working
Water heater working, at least 110 F, with the relief valve pipe extended to within 6 inches of the floor
Walls, ceilings and floors free of holes, chipped paint, cracks or stains; no rubbish inside or out
Doors and windows working with locks, screens on opening windows, one egress window in each sleeping area
Globe covers on closet and shelf lights; bathroom window or exhaust fan
Gutters, downspouts and roof sound; all plumbing working
Appliances working with an anti-tip bracket on the range; key locks on entry doors only
All utilities on at the inspection and no open construction permits

resale_co.how_to_apply: Fill in the Township of Pennsville Application for Continued Certificate of Occupancy, Residential Resale, and pay in full by certified check or money order payable to "Township of Pennsville" (or exact cash) at the Construction Code Office, 90 N Broadway. Applications can also be filed through the Township citizen portal (Apply for a Property Inspection, which needs a portal login). Inspections are Tuesday to Thursday, 3:00 to 5:30 PM.

resale_co.notes: The Township citizen portal says the Certificate of Continued Occupancy inspection is required when residential property is sold, and Chapter 7 (Sec. 7.4B-5) bars a buyer from occupying a dwelling without a certificate of occupancy. Fees: the resale form and the ordinance both give $50 for the first inspection. For later inspections the office form shows $50 for the re-inspection and $50 for the 2nd re-inspection, while the ordinance (Sec. 7.4B-9) lists "First inspection of above (for same certificate) $50.00" and "Second or subsequent inspection $100.00 per house/unit"; confirm which applies. Chapter 7 also sets a $160 fee for a construction-code certificate of continued occupancy under N.J.A.C. 5:23; that is a building-code certificate, not the resale housing inspection. The Township's "As Is" Document for Settlement (revised 11/14/22) lets a home be sold as-is: the buyer signs and notarizes it and must bring the home into compliance before anyone occupies it; that document says it becomes invalid 60 days from issue if the property is not purchased in that time, and lists P (856) 678-3089 ext. 143 and pvfirecode@pvtwp.com under Housing Official David Curry. No temporary certificate of occupancy is issued. Housing Officer email housingofficer@pvtwp.com is taken from the mailto link on his staff directory page; that page gives his extension as 1150 "for questions only". Rentals built before 1978 also need a lead-safe certificate (rental only).

requirements: Township handout asks for 10-year sealed battery smoke alarms on each level, in each bedroom and within 10 feet outside each sleeping area
Carbon monoxide alarm in the hallway within 10 feet of the bedrooms
Township handout still lists a 2A-10BC fire extinguisher (under 10 pounds) mounted within 10 feet of the kitchen, tagged or with a current receipt, top no more than 5 feet above the floor

authorities.how_to_apply: Not published separately. Smoke alarm, CO alarm and extinguisher checks are part of the Township resale housing inspection (Continued Certificate of Occupancy). Ask the Construction Code Office or the Fire Administrator whether a separate smoke/CO certificate and fee apply.

fire_cert.notes: Pennsville enforces the fire code itself (LEA registry code M; Chapter 14 names the Bureau of Fire Prevention and Inspections). The state fire directory (listed there as Pennsville Township 1708) names Fire Official Eric Guglielmo, (856) 678-3089, pvfireofficial@pvtwp.com, with "Pennsville Twp Fire Prev" for smoke detector compliance; the Township fire page lists him as Fire Administrator with pvfirecode@pvtwp.com and ext. 1144, which is used here as the newer official source. No separate smoke/CO certificate form or fee was found: the Township resale housing inspection checks smoke alarms, CO alarms and the extinguisher, and the Chapter 14 fee schedule covers only commercial and multi-unit inspections. The Township minimum requirements handout (undated) still includes the fire extinguisher and prints the pre-2025 text of N.J.A.C. 5:70-4.19; the state removed the extinguisher from the state requirement by P.L.2025, c.19, but the Township list still asks for it.

other_items.label: Taxes, sewer and water current
other_items.detail: No certificate of occupancy is issued unless Township taxes, sewer and water bills are current; for a change of ownership the Housing Officer may issue a conditional certificate with taxes paid by the settlement agent at closing.

other_items.label: No open permits or violations
other_items.detail: Documentation is needed that there are no outstanding open building permits, housing violations or court judgments barring occupancy; the resale form office section also checks open permits.

other_items.label: As-is sale option
other_items.detail: An "As Is" Document for Settlement (revised 11/14/22) lets the buyer take the home as-is, signed and notarized; the home must meet the property maintenance code before anyone occupies it.
